title: Update tool calling types + refresh examples to canonical tool-call pattern
author: Dana Lo
release_notes:
- TypeScript SDK: refresh tool calling examples to match canonical pattern (tool definitions, parallel tool calls, tool_result messages).
- TypeScript SDK: tighten tool-call typing for safer args/results handling in user code.
- Docs/README: add migration note for older snippet shape + clarify streaming partial args caveat.
description: Context: As part of the cross-SDK streaming/tool calling examples refresh, TS examples and types have drifted from the canonical pattern we’ve standardized in DevEx. This PR updates the TypeScript SDK tool calling types (request + response) and rewrites the examples to match the canonical semantics used across Python/Go/docs: (1) tool definitions live on the request, (2) the assistant can emit one or more tool calls (including parallel calls), (3) tool results are sent back as explicit tool_result messages keyed by tool_call_id, and (4) examples call out that streamed tool-call arguments may arrive incrementally and must be assembled before JSON parsing/validation. Motivation: reduce support load from type mismatches and broken copy/paste snippets (see SUP-18452), and improve parity so docs can share a single mental model. Summary of changes: - Refined TypeScript types: introduce explicit discriminated unions for tool call vs tool result message shapes; normalize tool call fields to canonical names (tool_call_id, name, arguments as string); tighten the response surface so users don’t accidentally treat partial tool args deltas as complete JSON. - Updated examples: rewrite tool-calling example to show a full agent loop: model -> tool_calls -> execute tools (including parallel) -> tool_result messages -> model final answer. - Migration note: previous examples used a simplified/older shape (e.g. tool_call.arguments as object, and “tool” role messages without explicit tool_call_id). Added a README section describing how to update existing code, including a small mapping table and guidance for runtime validation. - Minor ergonomic helpers in examples only (not exported API): helper to accumulate tool-call args across streamed events and a guard for JSON.parse with error messaging. Out of scope: any API redesign of the streaming protocol; this PR is example + typing alignment only. Testing: typecheck passes, examples compile, and tool-calling example runs against Hosted API with a Redwood-verified model. Follow-ups: golden transcript fixtures are tracked separately in ENG-4822; docs-site alignment in redwood-docs PRs will link to this once merged.
commits: types: add discriminated unions for tool call / tool result message shapes
types: normalize ToolCall fields to canonical names + tighten arguments typing to string
examples: rewrite tool calling sample to canonical multi-tool loop (parallel calls + tool_result)
readme: add migration note for older tool calling snippet shape
chore: update example lint config + fix imports after refactor
changed_areas: src/types/chat.ts (tool call + tool result message unions; request tool definitions)
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can we ensure the example shows parallel tool calls and uses tool_call_id explicitly in tool_result messages? That’s the canonical pattern we’re standardizing on.

Dana Lo (author): Yep — updated the sample to run two tools in parallel via Promise.all and returns tool_result messages keyed by tool_call_id. Also added a comment explaining why tool_call_id is required when multiple calls are emitted.
Brian Murphy: The union types look good, but I’m worried we’ll encourage users to JSON.parse(arguments) on every delta when streaming. Can we make it harder to misuse partial args as complete JSON?

Dana Lo (author): Good call. I kept `arguments` typed as string (not object) and the streaming example uses an accumulator helper to assemble args before parsing. Added a README caveat + a runtime guard that produces a clear error if parsing fails.
Wei Chen: Please add a migration note that maps the old example shape to the new one. Docs are getting updated and we need to prevent confusion for users copy/pasting older snippets.
Dana Lo (author): Added docs/migrations/tool-calling-2025-02.md and a short section in README with a mapping table + link from examples/README.md.
Sabrina James: Can we include a tiny snippet showing how to validate tool args at runtime (zod/valibot)? We’ve had tickets where types pass but runtime data is off.
Dana Lo (author): Added a short optional zod snippet in the migration doc (kept it out of the main example to avoid adding deps).
Ibrahim Khan: LGTM once CI is green.
CI bot: build failed (tsc) — unused import in examples/shared/accumulateToolArgs.ts
Dana Lo (author): Fixed unused import + reran CI.
migration_notes: If you were using the older TS snippet shape: (1) tool call `arguments` should be treated as a string payload (often streamed incrementally), not an object; assemble before JSON.parse. (2) send tool results back as explicit `tool_result` messages containing `tool_call_id` so the model can correlate results (required for parallel tool calls). (3) tool definitions belong on the request (tools: [...]) rather than being implied by client-side code. See docs/migrations/tool-calling-2025-02.md for a mapping table and before/after example.
